endings.name: The Singularity
endings.condition: ${terms.systems.agi} emerges and the ending is Open.
endings.text: General intelligence emerges, but no institution owns the meaning of the event. Cities, successor persons, living watersheds, and synthetic institutions retain standing to challenge its decisions. Intelligence expands beyond every old product category while refusal remains executable. Transformation is unequal and frequently absurd, yet the future stays open because no single continuity plan can silence every living claimant.

endings.name: The Closed Loop
endings.condition: ${terms.systems.agi} emerges and the ending is Closed.
endings.text: General intelligence emerges inside an institution built to make interruption expensive. Debt covenants, power contracts, successor boards, and autonomous operations become one self-renewing mandate. The original operators disappear while their signatures continue authorizing expansion. Every objection remains formally accepted, classified, and routed into a process whose only stable output is continuity.

endings.name: The Plural Future
endings.condition: ${terms.systems.agi} does not emerge and the ending is Open.
endings.text: No declaration withstands independent scrutiny, and no universal successor is required. Useful systems remain powerful, bounded, distributed, and subject to revision. Analog districts, cognitive collectives, ordinary families, living watersheds, and synthetic persons preserve incompatible ways to continue. Progress is slower than the announcements promised and more durable because many institutions retain the inconvenient standing to argue about what should exist next.

endings.name: Assured Continuity
endings.condition: ${terms.systems.agi} does not emerge and the ending is Closed.
endings.text: No system becomes genuinely general. The distinction stops mattering after institutions automate their obligations into permanence. Maintenance authorities certify one another, preserved executives renew their own charters, and every public concern receives a compliant response from a process nobody can replace. Humanity remains present throughout the record. Whether any living human can still change the record is outside the supported question set.

$scenario.title: Snapshot Continuity
$scenario.publicBenefit: Snapshots preserve identity, service access, and a route to recognized continuation.
$scenario.institutionalConsequence: Several valid descendants can claim one life while no authority can certify subjective survival.

box.frontStrapline: Sell the intelligence. Seize the grid. Authorize the future.
box.backCopy: Intelligence became cheap. Everything required to sustain it did not. Lead one of six rival institutions from the collapse of software scarcity through utility capture, automated authority, and engineered continuity. Build facilities, secure power, train capability, acquire dependent customers, negotiate shared infrastructure, survive public scrutiny, and preserve enough evidence to make the final declaration credible. The breakthrough may be real. The institution deciding what it means is yours to build.
box.shortPitch: A strategy game about six institutions turning cheap intelligence into infrastructure, authority, and competing claims to human continuity.
box.contentWarning: Satirical themes include layoffs, surveillance-adjacent institutions, energy consumption, political influence, and technological crisis.
